claims: Your casual loading, usually 25% on top of the base rate, stops.
whys: 25% is hard-coded rather than taken from EMPLOYMENT.casualLoading, and the same file has the hard-coded '21 days' and '6 months (12 months ...)' at lines 10-14 instead of EMPLOYEE_CHOICE values.

claims: Different pathways applied to some casuals up to 26 August 2025; the Fair Work Ombudsman explains the transitional rules.
whys: lib/constants/casual-conversion.ts records something different: eligible casuals employed before 26 August 2024 could first give notice from 26 February 2025 (not a small business) or 26 August 2025 (small business). The FAQ suggests a different pathway applied until that date, which the recorded source does not say. Check the wording against FWO's transitional rules.
constants: lib/constants/casual-conversion.ts (EMPLOYEE_CHOICE; add the transitional first-notice dates as constants)
reviewerNotes: The writer's question stands. casual-conversion-faqs.ts:42 says 'Different pathways applied to some casuals up to 26 August 2025'. lib/constants/casual-conversion.ts:29-32 records first-notice dates instead (26 Feb 2025 for employers that are not small businesses, 26 Aug 2025 for small business). Not changed.

claims: With a 25% loading, a full-time casual needs to be paid for about 41.6 weeks of the year ...
whys: 25% and 41.6 are hard-coded in the FAQ, but the page body works them out from EMPLOYMENT.casualLoading and compareCasualToPermanent (c.breakEvenWeeks). If the constant changes, the FAQ and the JSON-LD would drift.

claims: On weekends and public holidays most awards add the loading to the penalty rather than multiplying them
whys: This is a population claim ('most awards') with no figure or source on the page. Only the retail example backs it. Also, '1.25' and '187.5%' are hard-coded instead of coming from CASUAL_LOADING and RETAIL_PENALTIES.
reviewerNotes: The writer's question stands. casual-loading-faqs.ts:23 makes the population claim 'most awards add the loading to the penalty', and '1.25' and '187.5%' are hard-coded rather than taken from CASUAL_LOADING (lib/constants/junior-rates.ts) and RETAIL_PENALTIES. Not changed.

claims: Centrelink withholds tax at a rate you choose (or a default rate)
whys: Services Australia does not withhold tax from JobSeeker, Youth Allowance or Age Pension by default. Tax is withheld only if the recipient asks for a voluntary tax deduction, so '(or a default rate)' looks wrong. 'issues a Centrelink Payment Summary' may also need checking: the statement is now supplied through myGov and pre-filled to the ATO.
constants: none (hard-coded prose); confirm against Services Australia 'Tax and your payment' guidance
